rationale.headline: Brazil are a slight favourite to beat Japan (52% to win), though a tight low-scoring draw is very much in play (31.3%).

drivers.label: Attack vs defence
drivers.detail: Brazil's attack is projected for about 1.4 goals against Japan's defence, versus roughly 0.7 the other way — the scoring gap is what tilts the call.

drivers.label: Goal-creation strength
drivers.detail: Brazil carries the stronger end-to-end goal output in their FIFA match stats, so they convert more of their chances into the projected scoreline.

drivers.label: Low-scoring caution
drivers.detail: Both sides project to score few goals, and tight games like this end level more often than raw averages suggest — that keeps the draw alive at 31.3%.

rationale.methodNote: Market-blind: each team's FIFA on-pitch scoring rate (xG-for and goals-against, Bayesian-shrunk toward an Elo strength prior in the profile layer) is mapped to relative attack/defence strengths, combined via the Maher multiplicative model into per-team goal expectations on a neutral venue, then expanded into a Dixon-Coles score matrix with low-score dependence rho=-0.1 (league baseline 1.5 goals/side, goal scale 1); cell probabilities are collapsed to win/draw/win. No betting odds or prediction-market prices were used at any step.
